Pristinia_Deep_Location_Dossier.md · civic synthesis checked against the May 2024 assembly
body:
Pristinia is where Prima’s cosmic stakes become measurable. It needs defenses, harvest labor, winter stores, laws, festivals, and people willing to notice when a neighbor is carrying too much.

A settlement between older powers

By 30 August 2024, Melian Starguard described Pristinia as the chosen entry point into a cataclysmic regional struggle. The Rahu maintained an embassy in town, Eovar Harbor lay nearby, the Guardians of the Shard were to the south, and the ruins called The Before remained a threat in the surrounding woods. Pristinia was never only a quest hub; it was a vulnerable settlement between trade routes, dangerous places, and powers older than its present population.

Even the early archive speaks of people who had called Pristinia home “for a long time.” The current adventurers therefore entered an existing community rather than founding an empty one. Their importance grew as they became residents, workers, defenders, donors, and political actors whose choices could bring consequences back to the town.

The wall became history

In April 2024, adventurers—including Nienna—spent hours finishing Pristinia’s wall. In July an army struck it. The wall held a mighty blow because the players had built it; then sections began to fall. A routine community task returned three months later as material protection and emotional cost.

The assault also taught Delerium mechanically. Contamination made people feel stronger but less alive, while a haze fed on its energy, passed the defenses, and entered town. The siege engines were a distraction. The event ended; its contamination did not.

A town under ordinary pressure

Population growth overworks Farmer Frank and strains winter food. Inside the Common Man, Herb mentions dwindling dried fruit and an underworked farm. Aravil asks whether foraging can help; Tobias volunteers; a hunting expedition forms without a quest giver. Herb’s limit is as important as the need: take roughly twelve elk, not so many that next year’s herd is destroyed.

Belonging through usefulness

Aravil recognizes that hunting may be her place in the town. Skye refuses to exploit Lichen’s ignorance of money and makes an alarming stranger feel safe. Herb knows stores, habits, wages, and ecology. Pristinia is governed as much through local knowledge and mutual restraint as through spectacular heroism.

Rebuilding becomes ordinary · 2026

After zombie pirates burned the Common Man, its blackened frame remained visible while Pristinia rebuilt around it. By 3 July 2026, townsfolk were hauling charred beams, salvaging stone, bringing timber and nails, and spending resources donated by adventurers. The replacement was planned as a larger refuge for lost and wandering souls as well as old familiar faces; expensive cedar paneling was purchased to make another fire less likely, linking the civic project directly to Eovar when those materials were stolen there.

Pilgrim’s Hearth ultimately rose on the same foundations. By September 19 it was again a place where adventurers drank tea, socialized, and exchanged news. The Magic Academy was open: Marius and Aurélia studied under Scribonia, while Saoirse prepared material for her future turn teaching younger students. Thorn’s plan to bless the farm before returning to Gael adds a smaller but telling continuity—adventurers contributing directly to the harvest.

The open record

Pristinia’s eventual size, its political independence beside the Rahu, its relationship with the larger and rougher Eovar, and the durability of adventurer-built institutions remain unsettled. Its strongest continuity is not invulnerability but the practice of rebuilding without pretending destruction never happened.

Return to the Prima overview for the island’s public geography and the entrance to its protected ancient record.

The town as Ada remembered it

Ada’s civic chronicles preserve Pristinia’s changing emotional climate: early excitement over remarkable newcomers; quieter taverns after familiar defenders departed; the rise of businesses and factions; terror during the Rahu War; relief transformed into civic legend; and a later town made safer, harder, more organized, and less innocent by survival.

Those writings do not replace direct records of walls, battles, laws, or rebuilding. They preserve what physical chronology alone cannot: how those changes felt to people who had to keep living in the town afterward.

The road from the Gate

The town’s welcome begins before its walls. At the Gate, guides answer arrivals with shelter, orientation and choices about how to contribute. The road is also vulnerable: the siege-era accounts preserve smoke, attacks and a Rahu search party. Later, Vessalia’s welcome of Star shows the work continuing through a new generation of guides.

Ryvyt’s workshop

Ryvyting Creations, owned and operated by Ryvyt, brings a forge, magic-item crafting and spell trade into the town’s commercial life. It also serves the Ale-Chemy Knights’ shared work; ordinary retail later ceases during their shift toward Gael.

September–October · care, remembrance and unfinished work

Papirak’s funeral joins practical burial work with the town’s inheritance of a teacher. Scribonia promises to restore the Training Dungeon; Saoirse describes her educational aim; Pell finds purpose in trusted service.

Beyond town, an expedition returns herbs to Tabitha for Bogdan’s remedy. In October, graffiti honoring Swift Foot leads adventurers to Dasa asking for freedom. Each event produces new obligations whose outcome should remain open until later scenes establish it.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Tools for the fields

Gartina commissions six each of hoes, spades and pitchforks, plus three plow blades, from Jon. She favors durability over speed. Jon estimates forty gold and three weeks, with twenty-five gold for materials and fifteen for labor. The exchange records the commission and corrected materials deposit; it does not record delivery.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

The search reaches Roger’s house

In the Pristinia Haze investigation, Caravash searches Roger’s inherited house and hears labored breathing behind a basement door. They suspect the creature inside may be Roger, but this branch does not confirm its identity. Alayah calls for a coordinated response, Ryvyt transforms into Ryvytor, and the encounter returns to the main party record. The discovery is an investigative lead, not a separate quest or proof of Roger’s fate.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

The mansion misunderstanding ends

The McKalister mansion branch ends with Kevin explaining that he was protecting the family’s collectible haul. The family’s insects had complicated the welfare check; the supposed treasure proves to be boxed ornaments. After the misunderstanding is settled, the guard captain is taken to an abandoned sewer shack, and the infirmary receives several new gnome patients in the following weeks. This conclusion does not make the visitors’ conflicting earlier accusations reliable.

Scene evidence: 1, 2.

The town’s working places

The Archery Range passes skills between veterans, newcomers and families. The Walls preserve communal work and battle recovery. The Public Square brings exceptional decisions, public promises and changes of leadership before the town.

Kasiri tells a newcomer about the siege

Kasiri points to patchwork repairs while telling DogToy about flaming stones, displaced households sheltering with neighbors and Melian’s capture. She recalls a peace that spared both Pristinia and the Rahu from destruction. She also refuses to treat every individual Rahu as responsible for their leadership’s actions. The memories and that judgment retain Kasiri’s voice; they are not an omniscient account of every casualty or motive.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Protecting a town, sustaining a society

Pristinia’s civic work begins alongside its earliest expeditions. In the March 2024 quest record, Melian helps coordinate permanent settlement needs; Gartina connects population growth with food and cultivation; Quake calls for defences and a militia while reporting work on the roads. Medical supplies, usable land and capable hands already matter beside combat.

Later Ale-Chemy institutions, Tobias’s construction, Fenwick’s public work, teaching and the rebuilt Pilgrim’s Hearth extend that existing concern. Different people contribute at different times, and many roles overlap. The settlement’s history does not divide neatly into one group that protects and another that builds.

Victory can preserve a place without settling how people will eat, learn, work or share authority there. Pristinia’s civic history follows those continuing questions through an existing community whose residents and arrivals both shape its future.

Homes and the record of a town

Homes and households preserve changing residence, friendship and ownership claims. The Scroll Library preserves another form of continuity: shared spells, research and civic records that later residents can consult.

Early arrivals’ field notes · March 2024

The adventurer location notes preserves two early names. An entry posted on 7 March reports Melian Starguard calling the first village “The Settlement”; Scribonia’s entry of 8 March calls his base “The Homestead.” These are recorded usages, not evidence of an official renaming or proof that every early name had exactly the same boundaries.

Scribonia describes limited infrastructure and what he considers a poorly trained population near the portal. He proposes training civilians, constructing useful buildings and exploring outward. His assessment records an arrival’s priorities; it does not erase the community that already lived here or establish an objective development rank. The library, homes, walls and later civic institutions give those early ambitions a history beyond the note.

Read the campaign across its people

Pristinia · a town worth defending follows the choices, changing knowledge and consequences across this regional history. The unresolved record preserves the transitions still needing evidence.

Authority before the adventurers

In the May 2024 assembly record, Melian describes a council of three Elders, each elected by a majority of the settlement’s adults. Hiram, Magda and Kaja belong to this early civic order. In her account, Elders serve until death or step down because of infirmity or incapacity; they hear disputes and bear responsibility for the settlement’s welfare. This is a recorded form of local stewardship, not an adventurer monarchy or an assertion that every later office remains unchanged.

Melian’s work connects formal authority to everyday administration. She convenes discussion, explains procedure and gets decisions recorded. Wealth, spellcasting and success in battle do not by themselves grant an arrival the right to govern the people already living here.

Decisions that outlast the meeting

The assembly approves Hawthorne as secretary after Melian asks for someone to record proposals considered, rejected and approved, and to publish the resulting laws. The narrator records him counting votes twice. Written government grows through this practical work: separating what was proposed from what the community actually accepted.

Debate includes changing eligibility, terms of office and adventurers’ voting rights. A proposal preserved in the record is not automatically an enacted rule. The later Scroll Library, public records and household histories extend the same need for memory without making any single document a complete constitution.
